text:
lia: Quick heads-up — noticed a perf regression on the AWQ INT8 weight-only path in the dedicated cluster after yesterday's runtime change. KV cache hit rate dipped and tail p95 jumped.
jon: Where exactly? tags? model? :thinking:
lia: Model: redwood-7b-awq-int8 (serving alias: prod-7b-awq). Region: us-west-2-dedicated-1. Observed ~30% slowdown for 8k prompt workloads.
priya: Any profiling dumps? can you paste the flame or top hotspots?
lia: Pasted a short summary from perf-bot below — full flame linked in internal perf storage.
perf-bot: Kernel selection changed: preferred path -> int8_group_kern_v2, fallback rate increased to scalar_unroll (was 0.2% -> 3.6%).
KV cache: effective hit rate 98.1% -> 83.4% (aligned with more microbatches).
Pack overhead: avg pack/unpack CPU time per request 1.2ms -> 2.6ms.
Batcher: group prediction misfires increased, causing extra pack passes.
sam: That pack/unpack jump is suspicious — did the allocator change slab alignment? I remember a recent allocator tweak landed in eng-infra.
lia: Yeah, the allocator patch reverted the 64-byte alignment to 128 in certain slow paths. I suspect packing buffers are now crossing slab boundaries more often.
jon: Can you run a focused repro? config: packer.group_size, affinitize_kv, prefetch_stride. Also try forcing kernel_v1 to see delta.
lia: Running small repro now. Command: ```./run_infer --model prod-7b-awq --prompts sample_8k.json --batch-size 4 --group-size 128 --kv-affinity=auto --pack-mode=aggressive --profile=flame``` I'll share the flame link.
priya: Also try group_size=64 and group_size=32. AWQ group granularity interacts with packer; smaller groups sometimes reduce pack variance and kernel choice stability.
sam: For KV affinity test, set `--kv-affinity=cpu-local` vs `cpu-shared` to see cache locality. We saw ~12% improvement previously with cpu-local on hw rev B.
lia: Quick adhoc numbers from repro (wall clock average over 50 runs):
- baseline (pre-change, archived): p95=142ms, pack=1.1ms, KV-hit=98.1%
- current: p95=186ms, pack=2.6ms, KV-hit=83.4%
- force kernel_v1: p95=154ms, pack=2.5ms, KV-hit=84%
- group_size=32: p95=160ms, pack=1.9ms, KV-hit=91%
So reducing group size helps but doesn't fully recover baseline.
jon: Interesting that forcing kernel_v1 drops p95 a lot but pack still high -> suggests packer induced additional memcpy/zeroing not kernel choice. Could be allocator fragmentation plus more pack passes due to group splitting.
priya: Can you share the packer config you used? Also include the runtime flags for prefetcher.
lia: Current runtime flags: ```{"packer":{"mode":"aggressive","max_group_bytes":65536,"align":128}, "prefetch":{"enabled":true,"stride":8}, "kv":{"affinity":"auto"}}``` (that's from the test config)
sam: Try changing align back to 64 and prefetch.stride=4. Also test packer.mode=conservative to avoid repeated pack/unpack churn.
lia: Spun another run: packer.align=64 + stride=4 + group_size=64 -> p95=148ms, pack=1.3ms, KV-hit=95.6%.
priya: That looks very promising. If align=64 fixes pack overhead, we should revert allocator tweak for pack hotpath only or add a packer-specific allocation arena.
jon: For rollout: propose a canary that sets packer.align=64 on 10% of requests and monitors p95 and error rates. Also add a perf metric to track fallback->scalar kernel rate.
lia: I'll prepare a small canary config and a short deploy PR. @deploy-bot can you gate a canary for prod-7b-awq with the config snippet below?
```yaml
canary: true
percent: 10
overrides:
  packer.align: 64
  prefetch.stride: 4
  packer.mode: conservative
```
deploy-bot: Canary request received for prod-7b-awq, 10% traffic. Will schedule with observability hooks (p95, pack_ms, kv_hit, kernel_fallback_rate). ETA 20m.
lia: Thanks. I'll also open an eng-infra issue for allocator alignment change and propose a narrower fix (pack arena) + tests.
priya: Add a regression test into ci-perf that runs pack-heavy microbench with group_size sweep (32/64/128) and asserts pack/ms ratio not >1.5x baseline.
sam: +1. Also add a telemetry gauge for pack/unpack ops per request so we detect pack churn early.
jon: Nice triage. Great to see simple alignment tweak recovers most of it. Keep thread updated when canary metrics come in. :thumbsup:
lia: Will do — attaching flame link and raw perf dump: https://perf.internal/redwood/1755555555/flare (private).
